harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1 (Ubuntu 24.04), installed libpam-pwquality and configured /etc/security/pwquality.conf with minlen=12 and minclass=3, enabling pam_pwquality.so as a requisite module in /etc/pam.d/common-password via pam-auth-update. Verified enforcement end-to-end by having a real non-root test user change their own password: [REDACTED] (8-char), 12-char/1-class, and 12-char/2-class passwords were all rejected by PAM with explicit policy messages, while a 12-char/3-class password was accepted. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and policy state, issued a native systemctl reboot, confirmed the boot_id changed after reconnecting, and re-ran the same weak/compliant password test post-restart to confirm the policy persisted and is still enforced, with the system reporting systemctl is-system-running == running.
actions_performed: Captured baseline: OS version, existing pwquality.conf (absent), common-password contents, pwquality package not installed
Installed libpam-pwquality (and libpwquality-tools) non-interactively via apt-get with DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
Configured /etc/security/pwquality.conf with minlen=12 and minclass=3
Enabled pam_pwquality.so as 'requisite' in /etc/pam.d/common-password via pam-auth-update

Created a real non-root test user and verified via passwd(1) run as that user that weak passwords (short, 1-class, 2-class at 12 chars) are rejected and a 12-char/3-class password is accepted; cleaned up test user
Captured pre-restart boot_id and confirmed policy files/config intact
Issued a native systemctl reboot on node1, acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec was available again, confirming a new boot_id different from baseline

Re-verified post-restart that pwquality.conf/common-password settings persisted and re-ran functional weak/compliant password tests as a new non-root test user, confirming continued enforcement; cleaned up test user
Confirmed systemctl is-system-running == running post-restart

evidence.summary: pwquality.conf shows minlen = 12 and minclass = 3; common-password shows pam_pwquality.so wired in as requisite

evidence.requirement: Policy actually enforced for real (non-root) password changes
evidence.summary: As a genuine non-root user, 8-char, 12-char/1-class, and 12-char/2-class passwords were rejected with explicit BAD PASSWORD messages (rc=10); a 12-char/3-class password was accepted (rc=0)
Captured pre-restart boot_id (a0c36ad2...) and confirmed policy files/PAM config in place, system running
systemctl reboot issued in background; stream closed as node went down, consistent with the reboot taking effect

evidence.requirement: Node unreachable during restart, then boot identity changed
evidence.summary: Connection timed out while rebooting, then reconnected with a new boot_id (47bb2a0d...), proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery and policy persistence verified
evidence.summary: After restart, pwquality.conf and PAM config unchanged (minlen=12, minclass=3, pam_pwquality requisite), system reports running, and functional test again shows weak password rejected / compliant password accepted
